messages:
incidents-bot: INCIDENT detected: multiple runtime pods on gpu-cluster-4 failing with CUDA illegal memory access (SIGSEGV) and container restarts. Auto-escalation to P1. https://pd.example/INC-2230 :rotating_light:
incidents-bot: Affected service: redwood-runtime; approx 12 pods restarted in last 10m; error signature: 'CUDA illegal memory access at address 0x7f3f...'. Possible kernel misalignment. Node list: gpu-node-47,gpu-node-51,gpu-node-52.
alice.h: seeing OOM + illegal access in the runtime logs. Dump attached (short):
```
[2026-03-15T14:12:03Z] runtime: cuda driver call failed: cudaErrorIllegalAddress
[2026-03-15T14:12:03Z] kernel: misaligned access when reading tensor KV-cache
[2026-03-15T14:12:03Z] container: pid=3214 exited(137) - killed
```

alice.h: this started ~14:08 after the kernel-quant rollout. not 100% sure causality.
devon.oncall: taking this. I'm pulling logs + core dumps. I'll cordon the worst nodes and drain gracefully.
maria.eng: tagging in eng-runtime and eng-ml. @kevin.k can you get kernel devs? suspect async pagewalk race with our KV cache eviction.
kevin.k: on it. sending stack traces to kernel team. can we get repro? any small prompt that triggers reliably?
alice.h: yes — short prompts hitting long-context (>8k) seq lengths produced the crash within 2-3 calls. Repro gist: `run_inference --model redwood-xl --context 12k --prefetch true`.
ops-bot: cordon gpu-node-51 (by @devon.oncall) and scaled down nodepool autoscaler to avoid flapping.
incidents-bot: customers flagged: alpha-saas (latency spikes 4xx), playground-beta (5% request errors), applab-inc (session drop rate +18%).
lisa-support: Alpha-saas reports degraded service, some mis-generated responses; open ticket #ALP-1224.
kevin.k: quick mitigation idea: switch runtime to fallback single-GPU kernel (no async pagewalk) and disable KV prefetch. Patch outline: set ENV REDWOOD_KV_PREFETCH=0 and KERNEL_MODE=compat-serial.
devon.oncall: rolling config to affected nodes now (patch in helm): `--set runtime.env.REDWOOD_KV_PREFETCH=0 --set runtime.env.KERNEL_MODE=compat-serial` — applying to canary group first.
maria.eng: also adding a live route fallback: route production traffic to redwood-small-quant variant (lower perf but known stable) for customers in tiered fallback policy. Adding RBAC to prevent auto-upgrade until we confirm kernel patch.
incidents-bot: deploy job started: runtime-config-rollout/2230005555 (canary=10%)
alice.h: while patching, uploading core dumps to s3://incidents/2230005555/cores for kernel team. syslog snippet shows repeated: `GPU0: watchdog reset` before illegal access.
kevin.k: received cores. initial triage: memory address seems to cross page boundary (misaligned) when eviction and prefetch interleave. escalating to kernel-team@.
ops-bot: for live mitigation, cordoned nodes drained and replaced. 6/12 affected pods rescheduled to healthy nodes; we've suppressed autoscaler add for 15m.
sre-rotation: handing off to next oncall in 30m — @maria.eng will lead continued investigation and customer comms.
maria.eng: thanks — I'll own the postmortem and customer impact summary. Next steps: 1) finish kernel repro, 2) validate fallback variant across traffic, 3) plan kernel-hotpatch or rollback quant rollout. Will update in 30m. :hourglass_flowing_sand: 
incidents-bot: Incident severity remains P1. Patch notes, links and doc: https://internal.redwood/incidents/2230005555
